groups.title: Start here
groups.about: The two you will use most.

commands.title: Open this dashboard
commands.note: Starts the API and opens the dashboard in your browser, already signed in. Stop it with Ctrl+C.

commands.title: Run the tests
commands.note: Should end with a line like "284 passed".

groups.title: Simulated data, step by step
groups.about: Generate a labelled practice log and run it through the whole pipeline. Each step is safe to repeat.

commands.title: 1. Generate a practice log
commands.note: Writes data/demo.log and a label file saying which lines belong to which attack.

commands.title: 3. Add locations
commands.note: The impossible-travel rule needs these.

commands.title: 4. Run the rules and save the alerts
commands.note: Never erases a decision you recorded on an alert.

commands.title: Measure the rules across 50 simulations
commands.note: Prints the tables in docs/results.md. Takes about ten seconds.

groups.title: Live detection
groups.about: Follow a log as it grows. Alerts appear here within a couple of seconds.

commands.title: Follow a log file
commands.note: Prints ALERT and update lines as they happen. Run it in its own Terminal window; stop it with Ctrl+C.

commands.title: Send a fake attack to the followed log
commands.command: cd "{{project_dir}}" && NOW=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S) && for i in $(seq 0 11); do printf '%s.%06d+00:00 web01 sshd[1]: Failed password for root from 203.0.113.77 port 22 ssh2\n' "$NOW" "$i" >> data/demo.log; done
commands.note: Twelve failed logins stamped with the current time, so each run counts as newer than the last. Run it in a second window while the follower is running.

groups.title: Honeypot: from your Mac
groups.about: The honeypot keeps running whether or not you are connected.

commands.title: Log in to the honeypot server
commands.note: Asks for your key passphrase. The prompt changes to root@HoneyPot. Type exit to leave.

commands.title: Watch attacks arrive, in one step
commands.note: Any address that is not yours is a real visitor. Ctrl+C stops watching and disconnects.

groups.title: Honeypot data, step by step
groups.about: Real attack traffic goes in its own database, data/honeypot.db, apart from the practice data. The copied logs and the data folder both stay out of git.

commands.title: 1. Copy the honeypot's logs to this Mac
commands.note: Asks for your key passphrase. Copies into a folder outside the repo, and only adds what is new, so run it whenever you want fresh data. Never copy anything from the downloads folder: that is live malware.

commands.title: 2. Parse the logs into the honeypot database
commands.note: Safe to repeat after every copy: lines already stored are skipped. The list it prints shows what Cowrie logged that Siftlog does not turn into events. To leave out your own test logins, put your address in own_addresses in siftlog.local.json.

commands.title: 3. Run the rules and save the alerts
commands.note: Only the three honeypot rules can fire here. The ssh rules read real sshd logs.

commands.title: 4. Open the dashboard on the honeypot data
commands.note: Uses its own port, so it can run alongside a dashboard that is showing the practice data.

groups.title: Honeypot: after logging in
groups.about: Run these at the root@HoneyPot prompt.

commands.title: Is it running?
commands.command: systemctl is-active cowrie cowrie-redirect; ss -tln | grep ':2222 '
commands.note: You want active, active, and a LISTEN line.

commands.title: Who has visited
commands.note: Log entries per address, busiest first.

commands.title: Usernames and passwords tried
commands.command: grep -o '"message":"login attempt[^"]*"' {{honeypot_dir}}/var/log/cowrie/cowrie.json | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20

commands.title: Files uploaded or downloaded
commands.note: Each record has a shasum you can search for on VirusTotal. Search by hash only; never upload or open the file.

commands.title: Disk space and stored payloads
commands.note: Worth a look about once a week.

commands.title: Restart Cowrie
commands.command: systemctl restart cowrie && systemctl is-active cowrie
commands.note: Needed after changing its config. Down for a couple of seconds.

commands.title: Leave the server
commands.note: Only hangs up your connection. The honeypot keeps recording.
